title: The kingdom among you (Luke 17:20–37)
hookLine: the kingdom of God is within you, or in your midst

cards: When? Some Pharisees put it to Jesus straight: when will the kingdom of God come? When will things be put right, and God's reign be plain to see?
Under Roman rule, people longed for that day. It's a fair question. His answer is two verses long, and one tiny phrase in it can be read two ways.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you."
Not with observation: you can't track it like an astronomer watching for a comet. Don't chase people who say it's over here, or over there.
Then the tiny phrase, in Greek entos hymon. It can mean within you, inside each person. That's how the King James reads it, and Leo Tolstoy took a book title from it.

But it can also mean among you, in your midst, and other translations prefer that. Some readers point out that Jesus is speaking to people questioning him, and the one standing in front of them was Jesus himself.
On that reading, the kingdom is already in the middle of you, and you're asking when. Christians hold both readings. Some stress the inner life: God's reign begins in the heart.
Others stress the community and the person of Jesus: God's reign is happening right here, among people. Some hold the two together.
Then Jesus turns to his disciples and talks about a day that will come as suddenly as lightning, while people are eating, drinking, marrying, planting, as in the days of Noah and of Lot.
Three words of warning: "Remember Lot's wife." She looked back.
The passage holds two things together: the kingdom is already here, and still coming.

teach.h: THE KINGDOM OF GOD IS WITHIN YOU.
teach.b: The question was when. The answer points to where: already in the room.

how: Christians pray thy kingdom come every time they say the Lord's Prayer, and some churches speak of the kingdom as both already present and not yet complete, especially in Advent.

s: the Greek phrase can mean either within you or among you
entos hymon: the King James says within; other translations say among or in your midst.
Jesus tells people to follow anyone who says lo here, or lo there
"neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there!"
all Christians agree on one reading of this verse

games.q: some Pharisees ask Jesus when the kingdom of God will come. what does he answer?
o: it doesn't come with observation: it is within you, or among you.
games.why: "the kingdom of God cometh not with observation... for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you."

practice: Look around wherever you are, at the people near you or their traces, a photo, a chair someone sat in, and notice where there's kindness, patience or peace, even a little.
Then turn inward to one small good thing already growing in you; you don't have to make it, just notice it. If you pray, give thanks for it.

carryVoice: Your line: in your midst. Closer than the horizon, and still coming. Day five hundred sixty-four.
